## Overview

The SyncIgnore tool creates an ignore list that covers all development dependencies of a node.js package. These dependencies, which aren't needed on the robot won't be synced to the robot.

This is important under Node 6 (npm 3) because of the way the node_modules tree is organized. In Node 4, dependencies of a given package would always be found in that package's node_modules folder, with the same idea recursively applying to the dependencies of dependencies. Under Node 6, however, disk space is saved by putting commonly used dependencies as high as possible in the folder hierarchy. Thus, a commonly used dependency might reside in:

`/Users/ryanmcmahon/jibo/sdk/packages/jibo-gulp`

However, if two packages require different versions of a dependency, then one dependency's folder might be found higher in the folder tree, and another's further down. The require() function, when used in node.js code, begins by searching the immediate node_modules folder for the appropriate version of the requested package, then proceeds to climb up the tree (or down, if the tree is thought of in the arboreal sense :)).

SyncIgnore works in Node 4, too, because its algorithm functions more trivially with that package structure.

SyncIgnore generates an .syncignore-auto file, which contains a set of glob patterns, as needed to designate exclusions to rsync. These can take either a wildcard form, or directly reference a package, e.g.

```
**/node_modules/http
**/node_modules/url
**/node_modules/assert
**/node_modules/isparta
/node_modules/jibo/node_modules/glob
/node_modules/jibo/node_modules/jibo-anim-db/node_modules/mkdirp
/node_modules/jibo/node_modules/jibo-anim-db/node_modules/find-root
/node_modules/jibo/node_modules/jibo-anim-db/node_modules/jibo-keyframes/node_modules/fs-extra
/node_modules/jibo/node_modules/jibo-keyframes/node_modules/fs-extra
```

If an .syncignore-auto file already exists, SyncIgnore will simply load it and pass its contents on to the utility doing the actual syncing. Otherwise, it will perform a dependency search and create the .syncignore-auto file, which is a somewhat slower process.

## Command Line Interface

From any folder, one can run:

`node /Users/yourname/jibo/sdk/jibo-syncignore/tests/syncignore-cli.js`

This will generate an .syncignore-auto file, as described above.

Parameters:
* `--force`: force the regeneration of the .syncignore-auto file
* `--verbose`: prints a bunch of information about the search process to the console
* `--empty`: generates an empty .syncignore-auto file

### Other usage notes

From the command line, one can run:

`npm la --prod --parseable >depsProd.txt`

This generates a full list of production dependencies. If this file exists and syncignore-cli.js is run in `verbose` mode, it will note any cases where a production dependency is somehow flagged as a development dependency. This shouldn't happen and would be considered a fatal bug if it does.

## Use Cases

In all these cases, the user should not the importance of deleting the existing .syncignore-auto file, if an up-to-date one is needed.

### Skills Service Manager

The SSM code is synced to the robot using the script `./bin/run-on-robot.sh`. This script will run SyncIgnore under the hood.

### Be (or other) skill with npm run sync

`npm run sync` uses the './bin/sync.sh' script that lives in the be-framework package.

### Be (or other) skill with jibo sync

`jibo sync` uses the jibo-sync utility to sync files to the robot. This is the tool that third-party developers are meant to eventually use. It relies on the web server interface on the robot.

If the --regenerateAutoIgnore argument is set, the search will be run; otherwise, it will only be run if the .syncignore-auto file doesn't exist.
